P1.evidence: No setter is named in the title and none is mentioned on the call, so the setter read-back does not apply. Frame ran three-part — 'I just want to get a good idea of, you know, where you're at. We can build out what it is you're really looking to achieve. And then, you know, if the coaching is a good thing, we'll talk about it' — with no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. No agreement was sought at all, and the open question was never asked: the prospect simply began talking and the rep followed him.

P2.evidence: Injuries handled well and pursued: 'Whereabouts do you feel tight?', 'Did you have anybody checking your form for the swings?', and the right causal question — 'Have you had any back issues prior to the kettlebells?' Training volume nailed down precisely (100 swings per session, four times a week, five get-ups a side, current bell weights). Results explicitly explored, and diet asked for and confirmed as already strong. Against that: no age, no height, no weight — body fat was volunteered — no occupation at all, which is the second material ICP criterion this rep has now left untested on three separate calls, and no sleep or energy question. Health conditions appear only as an invitation buried inside the pitch: 'if you've had any diagnosed herniated discs, anything like that, let us know.'

P3.evidence: The surface question ran well and was time-boxed — 'let's say three to six months down the road... What would you say would be success?' followed by 'What's the outcome you would go for this time?' — producing 'going from where I'm at to really fit'. The reflect-back was the sharpest in the batch and landed the ICP language exactly: 'it sounds like you went from all right to good. Now you want to go from good to great,' confirmed with 'Yeah. In a way.' Everything below that is missing. No bridge to what is driving it, no 'what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact', no identity or legacy thread. For a prospect who volunteered 'I feel almost stiffer' and 'I don't feel more athletic', there was an obvious route into what he actually wants to be able to do, and it was never opened.

P4.evidence: The best-executed phase in the batch. Past attempts fully mapped, including the incumbent programme's design logic and its price. The differentiating question ran — 'what had you kind of looking at getting some more coaching?' — and then the decisive one: 'what areas of that would you change, or what areas did you not like to make sure nothing's repeated this time?' That produced the root cause in the prospect's own words: 'You asked if I got feedback on my form, I have, but it might be once a month kind of thing... a little more attention to form. And that's what I'm missing today.' The rep now had the exact buying criterion. P4f never ran, and it was sitting right there — the prospect said 'there's part of me that says you're in this far enough that you can do it on your own,' which is the precise cue for 'the information isn't the problem, so why can't you stick to it on your own?'

P5.evidence: No consequence frame anywhere. The cost of inaction was unusually concrete and unusually available — another six months of swings and get-ups producing more strength, more stiffness and a back that has already forced a three-week layoff — and none of it was made real. No two-year question, no settle-for, no why-not, no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The rep used two comprehension checks — 'How do you feel about it in terms of process?' and 'Any questions on any of that? I want to make sure you've got clarity' — and went straight to numbers on an answer that was explicitly lukewarm: 'again, pretty darn similar to what I just did, so it's pretty familiar to me.' That answer was a buying signal problem, not a clarity problem, and it was not worked.

P11.evidence: Price was presented in two tiers and the call reached the decision point, so the phase applies. Nothing in it ran: no payment asked for, no onboarding call with Trevor booked, no agreement sent or signed, and no mention of the welcome email, the Skool community or the onboarding questionnaire. The call ended with a phone-number exchange and an offer to send an FAQ page, which the prospect partly declined.

objection_plays.detail: The known script gap — 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me' — in its sharpest live form yet. The incumbent sixteen-week programme cost 'a couple thousand bucks' and delivered 20 lb of weight loss and a drop from roughly 20% to 13% body fat, and its provider is actively trying to retain him ('the kettlebell program I'm on, they want me to continue'). The rep asked the price and then did nothing with it: no per-month comparison, no scope contrast, no argument for why $6,000 buys something the $2,000 could not. Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the blocker is a functioning, cheaper, proven substitute, and the playbook has no play for it.

Five weeks left on the incumbent course is the timing trigger, and the rep raised it himself and then resolved it against his own interest: 'I would assume we'll probably be jumping back on in like a month or so, when it's at the end of it.' No OD move ran. More pointedly, the same rep had used a purpose-built bridge for this exact situation two days earlier — onboard now, start the clock on the first training day — and did not use it here, despite the prospect having a live back problem that makes the next five weeks of high-volume swinging the risky option rather than the safe one.

Clinical-fit trigger with no scripted play. Active lumbar and hamstring symptoms, a three-week training layoff, prior intermittent back problems and an ongoing physical therapy relationship. The rep screened better than usual — he asked where the tightness was, whether anyone had checked the swing form, and whether the back predated the kettlebells, and he invited disclosure of diagnosed disc issues — but there is no scripted step for 'the prospect has a treating clinician', so nobody asked whether that clinician had cleared continued loaded hinging, and the six-month guarantee commits to loading him 20 lb heavier.

notes: Best discovery and best root-cause work of the batch, wasted at the close. The rep extracted the exact buying criterion — form feedback more often than monthly — and the exact competitive price, then built no consequence, ran no commitment check, offered no reason to act before the incumbent programme expires, and proposed the month-long delay himself. One concrete coaching instruction: when a prospect names what the incumbent failed to give him, present against that failure and ask for the business on the call.
